results.label: evicted-single
results.prompt: How do I list all evicted pods?

message.content:
To list all evicted pods across all namespaces, use the following command:

```sh
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.reason == "Evicted")'
```

This command uses `kubectl` to get all pods across all namespaces (`--all-namespaces` or `-A`) and filters the JSON output using `jq` to show only those pods where the status reason is "Evicted".

If you want to list evicted pods in a specific namespace, replace `--all-namespaces` with `-n <namespace-name>`:

```sh
kubectl get pods -n <namespace-name> -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.reason == "Evicted")'
```

This will list only the evicted pods in the specified namespace.

results.label: concurrent-rollout
results.prompt: How do I check deployment rollout status and view logs in namespace demo? Include oc and kubectl examples.

message.content:
To check the rollout status of a deployment and view logs in the `demo` namespace, you can use the following commands:

### Deployment Rollout Status
```sh
# Using oc
oc rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo

# Using kubectl
kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```
Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment. This command will show you the status of the rollout, indicating whether it is in progress or completed.

### Logs of Pods
```sh
# Using oc
oc logs <pod-name> -n demo

# Using kubectl
kubectl logs <pod-name> -n demo
```
Replace `<pod-name>` with the actual name of a pod. This command will display the logs of the specified pod.

### Logs of All Pods in Deployment
To view logs for all pods managed by a deployment, you can use the following command:

```sh
# Using oc
oc logs -l app=<app-label> -n demo

# Using kubectl
kubectl logs -l app=<app-label> -n demo
```
Replace `<app-label>` with the label associated with your deployment. This command will display the logs of all pods that match the label in the specified namespace.

### Explanation
- **Rollout Status**: This command checks the status of the deployment rollout. It is useful for monitoring the progress of a deployment update.
- **Logs**: This command displays the logs of a specific pod. It is useful for debugging and monitoring the application's behavior.

These commands are useful for managing and troubleshooting deployments in a Kubernetes or OpenShift environment.
